youtube.baslik: Is every difference between two audiograms a fluctuation? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: Repeated measurements in the same person usually differ by five decibels or less; such small differences do not count as fluctuation. Repeated changes of ten decibels or more, in the same direction at adjacent frequencies, point more strongly to true fluctuation; bone conduction changing in the same direction as air conduction confirms that the change is sensorineural. Serial measurements use the same audiometer, the same earphones and the same method, and the timing of each measurement relative to an attack is recorded.
